title: FAR Module 2 · TBS 4

fields.label: 3. Carrying Amount at End of Year 3 Before Impairment

html:
TASK-BASED SIMULATION

Equipment Acquisition, Depreciation & Impairment

Determine the capitalized cost of equipment, calculate depreciation and analyze whether an impairment loss should be recognized.

Scenario

Atlas Corp. purchased production equipment on January 1 for a quoted price of $180,000.

Atlas incurred the following additional costs:

Freight $6,000
Installation $9,000
Testing Before Use $5,000
Annual Maintenance Contract $4,000

The equipment has an estimated useful life of 10 years, an estimated residual value of $20,000, and Atlas uses straight-line depreciation.

Impairment Information

At the end of Year 3, after recording Year 3 depreciation, adverse business conditions indicate that the equipment may be impaired.

The sum of the expected undiscounted future cash flows from the equipment is $130,000.

The equipment's fair value at that date is $118,000.

Required

1. Capitalized Cost of Equipment
2. Annual Straight-Line Depreciation
3. Carrying Amount at End of Year 3 Before Impairment
4. Impairment Loss
explanation:
Step 1 — Capitalized Cost

Costs necessary to acquire the equipment and prepare it for its intended use are included in the asset's cost.

Purchase Price $180,000 + Freight $6,000 + Installation $9,000 + Testing $5,000 = $200,000

The $4,000 annual maintenance contract is a period expense and is not capitalized as part of the equipment.

Capitalized Cost: $200,000

Step 2 — Annual Depreciation

($200,000 − $20,000) ÷ 10 Years = $18,000

Annual Depreciation: $18,000

Step 3 — Carrying Amount After 3 Years

Accumulated Depreciation: $18,000 × 3 = $54,000
$200,000 − $54,000 = $146,000

Carrying Amount: $146,000

Step 4 — Impairment Test

Because impairment indicators exist, Atlas first performs the recoverability test.

Carrying Amount: $146,000 > Undiscounted Future Cash Flows: $130,000

Because the carrying amount exceeds undiscounted future cash flows, the asset is not recoverable and an impairment loss must be recognized.

Carrying Amount $146,000 − Fair Value $118,000 = $28,000

Impairment Loss: $28,000

CPA Takeaway

  • Capitalize costs necessary to acquire an asset and prepare it for use.
  • Ordinary recurring maintenance is generally expensed.
  • For long-lived assets held and used, first test recoverability using undiscounted cash flows.
  • If the asset is not recoverable, measure the impairment loss using fair value.
